fixes.explanation: Good thinking, but Jesus never asks about the sacrifices. Some of those present tell Him what happened, and He asks whether those Galileans were "…worse sinners than all the other Galileans…" That's the question He puts to them. I think this one is heavy, friend.

It's a fair thing to wonder, but Jesus doesn't ask it. Pilate comes up only because some of those present tell Jesus what happened (Luke 13:1). Jesus asks about the Galileans themselves: were they "…worse sinners than all the other Galileans…"? I think this one is heavy, friend.

That's right. Jesus asks whether they were "…more sinful than all the others living in Jerusalem?" and He answers, "No, I tell you." I think this one is heavy, because eighteen people died when the tower of Siloam collapsed on them. Then He gives the same warning He just gave.

It's the other way around. Jesus says about the eighteen, "No, I tell you." They were not more sinful than all the others living in Jerusalem. I think this is a heavy part, friend. What He says next is the warning about repenting.
Yep. The man "…went to look for fruit on it but did not find any." Not a little, and not some. The tree is planted in his vineyard, and that's where he looks.

That would be a different parable. Here the man "…did not find any." A few small figs? Friend, this tree didn't hand him even one. I'd settle for one lonely fig to show off like a trophy, but there wasn't even that.
No birds show up in this parable. The man "…did not find any" fruit to begin with. Nothing pecked and nothing picked, friend, because he found none.

Moving the tree isn't what the owner says. His order is "Therefore cut it down!" He doesn't ask for a new field or a new spot. A tree that gets relocated instead of the ax would be the luckiest tree around, friend, but that's not in this parable.
A month is shorter than what he asks for. The keeper says, "leave it alone again this year…" It's a year, friend, and later he even says "next year" (Luke 13:9). So the blank needs year, not month.
A decade is way too long. The keeper asks for "…again this year…" and then he talks about "next year." Ten years is a whole lot more than he asks for, friend. The word he uses is year.
No fence in this parable. The keeper says, “…until I dig around it and fertilize it.” Digging and fertilizing is all he mentions. A fence never comes up.
